state.case_summary:
A man in his 60s presented with an enlarging purpuric patch on his left lateral superior forehead and left anterior scalp, initially present for 2 weeks. Further discussion revealed the lesion first developed in March 2014 and was fairly stable until June 2014, when there was rapid growth and extension followed by central ulceration and bleeding.

Clinical examination revealed a 30 × 25-cm centrally eroded purpuric plaque with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules involving:- Left anterior scalp with extension posteriorly on left parietal scalp- Superior aspect of left occipital scalp- Anteriorly on left forehead and left lateral cheek- Medially to right frontal and right parietal scalpNo evidence of lymphadenopathy in preauricular, cervical, occipital, submandibular or supraclavicular areas.

{'Biopsy & Histopathology': '- Dermis permeated by irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes and lined by plump oval cells- Cells had pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei- Cells stained positively with CD31 and were negative for CK5- Strong immunopositivity for ADRB1, ADRB2, and ADRB3 receptors- Ki-67 proliferation marker analysis performed', 'Imaging Studies': '- Chest and abdominal CT scan with contrast (June 2014): No evidence of nodal, pulmonary, or liver metastases- Staging: T2N0M0'}

What is the most likely diagnosis?

Options:
A. Kaposi sarcoma
B. Angiosarcoma
C. Pyogenic granuloma
D. Cutaneous angiosarcoma

static_evidence_items.content: Chief complaint: enlarging purpuric patch on left lateral superior forehead and left anterior scalp
Duration of lesion: initially present for 2 weeks, first developed in March 2014
Lesion characteristics: rapid growth and extension followed by central ulceration and bleeding in June 2014
Clinical examination findings: 30 × 25-cm centrally eroded purpuric plaque with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules
Locations of lesions: left anterior scalp, left parietal scalp, left occipital scalp, left forehead, left lateral cheek, right frontal scalp, and right parietal scalp
No evidence of lymphadenopathy in preauricular, cervical, occipital, submandibular, or supraclavicular areas
Biopsy findings: dermis permeated by irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes and lined by plump oval cells
Biopsy findings: cells had pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei
Immunohistochemistry: cells stained positively with CD31 and were negative for CK5
Immunohistochemistry: strong immunopositivity for ADRB1, ADRB2, and ADRB3 receptors
Imaging studies: chest and abdominal CT scan with contrast (June 2014) showed no evidence of nodal, pulmonary, or liver metastases
